series.note: Onboarding follow-up; client sets out a balanced, moderate, long-term mandate around Swiss blue chips, healthcare and some US tech.
First portfolio review; client pleased with steady performance and comfortable holding the balanced allocation.
Client raises equity concentration and an interest in broadening into real assets and alternatives.
Volatility prompts mild de-risking; client first raises his art collection and wine cellar as possible wealth.
Brief check-in; client wary of headlines and unwilling to add new risk, preferring to hold quality.
Client first voices unease about the size of the tech position and is open to trimming concentration gradually.
Client signals a clearer preference for stability over growth and asks to keep tilting toward steadier holdings.
Summer volatility nudges the client further toward protection; reaffirms ESG preferences alongside a low-beta, quality stance.
Client crosses into a conservative stance, prioritising capital preservation and ESG over higher-beta tech.
Client firmly confirms the conservative, preservation-first stance and asks for ballast uncorrelated with equities.
